title: Extra passive delay cannot reproduce two broad ASASSN-14ko UV flare fits on a fixed clock
abstract: We test whether extra passive delay can change a narrow ASASSN-14ko UV flare into the broad fitted flares of cycles 28 and 29. A causal response that conserves fluence cannot increase the cumulative normalised fluence. Against the published cycle-21 UVW2 profile on the constant X-ray clock, an arbitrary added component must supply at least 25.8 and 18.2 percent of broad flare fluence. Conditional central 95 percent ranges of these lower bounds are 20.0-31.0 and 12.2-25.3 percent. Cycle 20 gives similar results. The less certain cycle-30 reference is inconclusive for cycle 29. Clock shifts and added late fluence weaken the bounds. The test permits time-dependent nonnegative delay and passes independent finite transport checks. It extends the fallback-stretch test to passive delay. The result depends on fitted profiles, clock alignment and use of a narrow observed profile as input. Earlier fuel, stored energy, changing UV efficiency and two different causal responses can evade it. It does not establish an orbital change. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure are supplied.

display.caption: Cumulative fitted UVW2 fluence and the lower bound on an added component. Bands and error bars show conditional central 95 percent posterior ranges. Clock alignment and profile model are fixed.
